Definition: from G5259 and G2983; to take from below, i.e. carry upward; figuratively, to take up, i.e. continue a discourse or topic; mentally, to assume (presume):--answer, receive, suppose.
BiblicalUsage: Scripture uses hypolambánō where we would say to suppose, to take up, to answer. In Luke 7:43, the text says "Simon answered and said." In Luke 10:30, the text says "And Jesus answering said."
TheologicalSignificance: I believe hypolambánō shows us that wisdom begins with fearing the Lord, and it shows in how we live, not just what we know. That shapes how I read the passages where it appears: not as filler, but as God's own wording for what He is doing.
RelatedEvents: The Good Samaritan; The Ascension; The Sinful Woman Anoints Jesus
